mainTopic: The גמרא's list of folk remedies: heart problems (with רבינא's correction), bowels and worms, the spleen, hemorrhoids, bladder stones, and fevers
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's long list of folk remedies. It finishes a remedy from the previous amud. Then it gives cures for a stinging pain, for drinking uncovered water (גילוי), for a pus-filled wound, and for several heart problems. רב אחא מדיפתי objects that רבינא's barley remedy would make a racing heart worse. רבינא answers that he said it for heaviness of the heart, and he gives a wheat-and-honey remedy for a racing heart. The list goes on with cures for intestinal pain and worms, and wet or dry chamomile for the bowels. Then comes a long 'if not' ladder of spleen cures, ending with a barrel of wine; רב אחא בריה דרבא suggests eating bread every morning instead. Next come cures for hemorrhoids, rheumatism, and a bladder stone. The amud ends with fevers: a sweat bath for an external fever, and a cure for an internal fever that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the remedy: cabbage stalks, marjoram, and a backup option
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a remedy that started earlier. It explains how to prepare it, gives a backup if that is not possible, and adds a warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: Drip the mixture onto three cabbage stalks and stir it with a sprig of marjoram. When the marjoram sprig is cooked, the whole thing is cooked. If you can't do this, take the dung of a white dog and knead it with balm. As much as you can, don't eat the dung itself, because it loosens the limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of a remedy that began just before this part. It finishes the instructions, gives a backup cure, and adds a safety warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The marjoram sprig works like a timer: once it is cooked, you know the whole mixture is ready. The backup cure comes with a limit: use the dung mixture, but avoid actually eating the dung, because it is harmful.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not: introduces a backup option

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a remedy. The word 'it' at the beginning refers to the mixture described at the end of the previous amud, not to something new.

phrases.english: and let him drip it onto three stalks of cabbage,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the mixture from the remedy that began at the end of the previous amud.

phrases.english: and stir it with a sprig of marjoram;
and when the sprig of marjoram is cooked,
all of it is cooked.
And if not,
let him bring the dung of a white dog,
and knead it with balm.
And as much as possible,
let him not eat the dung, because it loosens [the limbs].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a remedy begun in the text just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prepare the mixture on cabbage stalks and stir with marjoram until cooked. If that is not possible, use white dog dung kneaded with balm, but avoid eating the dung itself.

steps.title: Remedy for a stinging pain
steps.stepSummary: For גירא, a sharp, stinging pain, use water poured over a stone called an 'arrow of Lilith.' The backup is water a dog drank from at night, with a warning about uncovered water.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a stinging pain: take an 'arrow of Lilith,' turn it over, pour water on it, and drink. If you can't, take water that a dog drank from at night. But be careful about water that was left uncovered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new remedy, for a stinging pain. It gives a main cure, a backup cure, and a warning that comes with the backup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The backup cure uses water left out at night, which raises a danger: water left uncovered may have been drunk from by a snake. So the גמרא adds a warning about גילוי, uncovered water, and that warning leads straight into the next remedy.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'arrow'; here, a sharp, stinging pain
'Arrow of Lilith,' the name of a kind of stone
Uncovered water, a liquid left exposed and possibly made dangerous

steps.whyThisMatters: The warning about uncovered water connects to the well-known concern of גילוי, which is why the גמרא immediately gives a cure for it.

phrases.english: For a stinging pain,
let him bring an 'arrow of Lilith,'
phrases.notes: This is the name of a kind of stone.

phrases.english: and turn it over,
and pour water on it and drink.
And if not,

phrases.aramaic: לַיְתֵי מִמַּיָּא דְּאִישְׁתִּי מִינַּיְיהוּ כַּלְבָּא בְּלֵילְיָא;
phrases.english: let him bring some of the water that a dog drank from at night;
and let him be careful about uncovered water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next ailment in the list of remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a stinging pain, drink water poured over an overturned 'arrow of Lilith.' Otherwise, drink water a dog drank from at night, but beware of uncovered water.

steps.title: Remedy for drinking uncovered water
steps.stepSummary: The cure for someone who drank uncovered water is a quarter-לוג of undiluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: For uncovered water: a quarter-לוג of undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last step warned about uncovered water, the גמרא now gives the cure in case someone drank it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This remedy follows directly from the warning in step 2. The cure is strong, undiluted wine, in a set amount.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter-לוג, a set liquid measure

phrases.english: For uncovered water,
a quarter-log of undiluted wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the warning about גילוי from step 2 and gives its cure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever drank uncovered water should drink a quarter-לוג of undiluted wine.

steps.title: Remedy for a pus-filled wound
steps.stepSummary: For a מורסא, a pus-filled wound, drink a quarter-לוג of wine with red ice plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a pus-filled wound: a quarter-לוג of wine with red ice plant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to another ailment, a pus-filled wound, and gives a wine-based cure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure uses the same measure of wine as the last one, a quarter-לוג. This time it is steeped with a plant, red ice plant.

keyTerms.meaning: Red ice plant, a kind of plant

phrases.english: For a pus-filled wound,
a quarter-log of wine, with red ice plant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list of remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a pus-filled wound, drink a quarter-לוג of wine steeped with red ice plant.

steps.title: Remedy for a racing heart
steps.stepSummary: For פירחא דליבא, a racing heart, eat three barley loaves soaked in fresh כמכא, then drink diluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a racing heart: take three barley loaves, soak them in כמכא that is less than forty days old, and eat them. Then drink diluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for a heart that beats too fast. This remedy is about to be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three details: three barley loaves, כמכא less than forty days old, and diluted wine afterward. These heavy foods are exactly what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'flying of the heart'; palpitations, a racing heart
A kind of food preparation used for soaking

phrases.english: For palpitations of the heart,
let him bring three loaves of barley,
and soak them in kamka
over which forty days have not passed,
and let him eat;
and let him drink diluted wine after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְפִירְחָא דְלִיבָּא לַיְתֵי תְּלָת בְּרוֹשִׁיָּיאתָא דִשְׂעָרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the list; this is the remedy that will be challenged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a racing heart, eat three barley loaves soaked in fresh כמכא and drink diluted wine afterward.

steps.title: Wouldn't this make the heart race even more?
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדיפתי objects to רבינא that these foods would make a racing heart worse, not better.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא מדיפתי said to רבינא: All the more so his heart will race!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדיפתי challenges the heart remedy as רבינא taught it. He argues that these foods would make the heart race even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is logical: a cure should calm the problem, but these foods would make it worse. So the remedy as it was said seems to work against its own purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from the town of Difti
An אמורא who taught this remedy

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Acha of Difti said to Ravina:
All the more so his heart will race!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּיפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן דְּפָרַח לִיבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the remedy given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The remedy for a racing heart in step 5
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Barley loaves, כמכא and wine would make the heart race more, so they cannot cure a racing heart.

steps.title: The remedy was for heaviness of the heart
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that he never said the remedy was for a racing heart. He said it for heaviness of the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I said it for heaviness of the heart.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge by correcting which illness the remedy is for. He says it was meant for a heavy heart, not a racing one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The remedy itself stays the same; only the illness it treats changes. For a heavy, sluggish heart, foods that stir the heart up make sense, so the challenge goes away.
steps.whatToRemember: רבינא's heart remedy (barley loaves, fresh כמכא, diluted wine) is for heaviness of the heart, not a racing heart, because these foods would make a racing heart worse.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not taking back the remedy. He is only correcting which illness it was meant for.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I said it for heaviness of the heart;

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲנָא לְיוּקְרָא דְלִיבָּא אֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא מדיפתי's challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting which illness the remedy is for
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The remedy was for a racing heart, so these foods would make it worse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The remedy was said for heaviness of the heart, where these foods are helpful.

steps.title: The real remedy for a racing heart
steps.stepSummary: For פירחא דליבא, eat three wheat loaves soaked in honey, then drink undiluted wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a racing heart: take three wheat loaves, soak them in honey, eat them, and then drink undiluted wine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא keeps answering: after saying his earlier remedy was for heaviness of the heart, he gives the correct remedy for a racing heart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא מדיפתי objected that barley and כמכא would make a racing heart worse. The remedy given here swaps them for wheat and honey, foods that fit his objection. So the earlier exchange is completed: each heart problem now has its own cure.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 5. That remedy (barley and כמכא) was for heaviness of the heart. This one, with wheat and honey, is for a racing heart.

phrases.english: For a racing heart:
let him bring three loaves of wheat,
soak them in honey, and eat them,
and drink undiluted wine after them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the clarification in step 7, this gives the correct remedy for the condition רב אחא מדיפתי asked about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A racing heart is treated with three wheat loaves soaked in honey, followed by undiluted wine.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two different heart conditions. Heaviness of the heart gets barley and כמכא, and a racing heart gets wheat and honey.

steps.title: Remedy for heart pain
steps.stepSummary: For צרחא דליבא, eat three egg-sized portions of mint, one of cumin, and one of sesame.
steps.simpleTranslation: For heart pain: take three egg-sized amounts of mint, an egg-sized amount of cumin, and an egg-sized amount of sesame seeds, and eat them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to a new heart problem and gives its remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a third heart condition, separate from heaviness and from racing. The cure is measured in egg-sized portions: three of mint and one each of cumin and sesame.

phrases.english: For heart pain:
let him bring three egg-sized amounts of mint,
and an egg-sized amount of cumin,
and an egg-sized amount of sesame seeds, and let him eat them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of remedies with a different heart condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Heart pain is treated by eating mint, cumin, and sesame in egg-sized amounts.

steps.title: Remedy for intestinal pain
steps.stepSummary: For כאב מעי, take three hundred long peppers and drink one hundred of them in wine each day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For intestinal pain: take three hundred long peppers, and each day drink one hundred of them in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for pain in the intestines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure lasts three days: three hundred peppers in total, one hundred a day, taken in wine.

phrases.english: For intestinal pain:
let him bring three hundred long peppers,
and every day let him drink
one hundred of them in wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of remedies with an intestinal condition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Intestinal pain is treated with three hundred long peppers, one hundred a day in wine.

steps.title: The story of רב אשי's daughter being healed
steps.stepSummary: רבין דמן נרש prepared one hundred fifty local peppers for רב אשי's daughter, and she was healed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין of נרש made it for רב אשי's daughter with one hundred fifty of our local peppers, and she was healed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story showing the pepper remedy actually working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story supports the remedy from step 10 with a real case. It also adds a detail: with 'our' local peppers, one hundred fifty were used instead of three hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: רבין from the town of נרש

phrases.english: רבין of נרש
prepared it for the daughter of רב אשי:
one hundred and fifty of these of ours,
phrases.notes: 'Ours' means the local peppers where they lived, and only half the number was used.

phrases.english: and she was healed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִין דְּמִן נָרֶשׁ עֲבַד לַהּ לְבַרְתֵּיהּ דְּרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up the pepper remedy of step 10 with a real case.
steps.raayaObject: The pepper remedy for intestinal pain.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story in which רבין דמן נרש healed רב אשי's daughter using one hundred fifty local peppers.

steps.title: Remedy for roundworm
steps.stepSummary: For כירצא, drink a quarter-לוג of wine steeped with laurel leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: For roundworm: a quarter-לוג of wine with laurel leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for an intestinal worm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure uses the same amount of wine, a quarter-לוג, as the cure for uncovered water in step 3. Here the wine is steeped with laurel leaves.

phrases.english: For roundworm:
a quarter-לוג of wine
with laurel leaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of remedies with intestinal worms.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roundworm is treated with a quarter-לוג of wine steeped with laurel leaves.

steps.title: Remedy for white worm, with a safety warning
steps.stepSummary: For כירצא חיורא, tie cress in cloth, soak it in water, and drink. Be careful not to swallow the seed, or it can puncture the intestines.
steps.simpleTranslation: For white worm: take cress and wrap it in a piece of cloth, soak it in water, and drink it. Be careful with the seed, because if not, it will puncture his intestines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a cure for a second kind of worm and adds a warning about how to take it safely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cress is wrapped in cloth so only its water is drunk. The warning explains why: if a seed gets through, it can damage the intestines.
steps.whatToRemember: These remedies come in a list. Each one names a condition and then gives its cure, and some add a story or a safety warning.

phrases.english: For white worm:
let him bring cress
and tie it up in a woven cloth,
and soak it in water and drink it;
and let him be careful with the seed,
for if not, it will puncture his intestines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the remedy for roundworm, this gives the remedy for a second kind of worm.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: White worm is treated by drinking water in which cress, tied in cloth, was soaked, while taking care not to swallow the seed.

steps.title: Chamomile to bind or loosen the bowels, with a memory sign
steps.stepSummary: Wet chamomile stops diarrhea, and dry chamomile soaked in water loosens the bowels. A memory sign helps keep the two apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: To stop the bowels, use chamomile while it is wet with water. To loosen them, use dry chamomile in water. Your sign: wet grass is what dams up a river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives two opposite remedies made from the same plant. It adds a memory trick so you don't mix them up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plant is the same in both cures. Only its condition changes: wet chamomile binds, and dry chamomile soaked in water loosens. The sign works because wet grass is used to block a river, just as wet chamomile blocks the flow of the bowels.

keyTerms.meaning: To bind, meaning to stop diarrhea
To loosen, meaning to relieve constipation

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip the two cures. WET chamomile is the one that stops things up, like wet grass damming a river.

phrases.english: To bind the bowels: chamomile that is wet with water.
To loosen the bowels: dry chamomile in water.
And your sign: wet grass, which dams up a river.
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are the corrected spelling of the word for 'wet'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of remedies from step 13, now for binding and loosening the bowels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wet chamomile binds the bowels. Dry chamomile soaked in water loosens them. Mnemonic: wet grass dams a river.

steps.title: Leeches in wine as a remedy for the spleen
steps.stepSummary: For a spleen illness, dry seven leeches in the shade and drink two or three of them in wine each day.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the spleen: bring seven leeches, dry them in the shade, and every day drink two or three of them in wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: cures for the spleen. This is the first and main remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first option is the main cure. The steps that follow each begin with 'and if not', so they are backup cures for someone who cannot do this one.

phrases.english: For the spleen: let him bring seven leeches
and dry them in the shade,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל יוֹמָא נִישְׁתֵּי תַּרְתֵּי וְתִלְתָּא בְּחַמְרָא.
phrases.english: and every day let him drink two or three of them in wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bowel remedies to a new illness, the spleen.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the spleen, dry seven leeches in the shade and drink two or three daily in wine.

steps.title: Backup cure: drying a goat's spleen while saying a formula
steps.stepSummary: If the leeches can't be used, dry a young goat's spleen in an oven while saying a formula. Or place it between the bricks of a new house and say the same words.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring the spleen of a goat that has not given birth, put it in the oven, and stand facing it. Say: 'Just as this spleen dries, so may the spleen of so-and-so son of so-and-so dry.' If not, put it between the bricks of a new house and say the same thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second-choice spleen cure, and then a third choice that uses the same goat spleen in a different place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This cure works by comparison. As the goat's spleen dries out, the sick person's swollen spleen should shrink too. The new-house version keeps the same spleen and the same words; it only changes where the spleen is dried.

keyTerms.meaning: So-and-so son of so-and-so (fill in his name and his mother's name)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – לַיְתֵי טְחָלָא דִצְיפִרְתָּא דְּלָא אִיפְּתַח,
phrases.english: And if not, let him bring the spleen of a female goat that has not given birth,
and place it in the oven, and stand facing it,
and say: 'Just as this spleen dries,
so may the spleen of so-and-so son of so-and-so dry.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – נִיטְחֲיֵיהּ בֵּינֵי אוּרְבֵי דְבֵיתָא חַדְתָּא,
phrases.english: And if not, let him place it between the bricks of a new house,
and say the same thing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא – לַיְתֵי טְחָלָא דִצְיפִרְתָּא דְּלָא אִיפְּתַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives backup options for someone who cannot use the leech remedy of step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry a goat's spleen in an oven, or between the bricks of a new house, while saying the drying formula.

steps.title: Backup cure: the hand of someone who died on שבת
steps.stepSummary: If not, place the hand of a person who died on שבת on the spleen and say a similar drying formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, look for a dead person who died on שבת. Take his hand, place it on the patient's spleen, and say: 'Just as this hand dried up, so may the spleen of so-and-so son of so-and-so dry.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another backup spleen cure, built on the same 'just as this dries' pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern is the same as in step 16, but now a dead person's dried-out hand takes the place of the goat's spleen. The text says the person must have died on שבת but does not explain why.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא, לִיבְקֵי שָׁכְבָא דִּשְׁכֵיב בְּשַׁבְּתָא,
phrases.english: And if not, let him search for a dead person who died on שבת,
and take his hand and place it on his spleen,
phrases.notes: 'His spleen' here means the sick person's spleen, not the dead person's.

phrases.english: and say: 'Just as this hand dried up,
so may the spleen of so-and-so son of so-and-so dry.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא, לִיבְקֵי שָׁכְבָא דִּשְׁכֵיב בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next backup option in the 'and if not' chain of spleen remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Place the hand of someone who died on שבת on the spleen and say the drying formula.

steps.title: Backup cure: fish and water from a blacksmith's shop
steps.stepSummary: If not, roast a fish in a blacksmith's shop, eat it with the blacksmith's water, and drink that water too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring a fish and roast it in a blacksmith's shop. Eat it with the water from the blacksmith's shop, and drink from that water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another backup spleen cure. This one has no formula to say; it uses the blacksmith's water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key ingredient is the blacksmith's water, the water used to cool hot metal. The next step brings a story to show that this water really affects the spleen.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – נַיְתֵי בִּינִיתָא וְנִיטְוְויֵיהּ בֵּי נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: And if not, let him bring a fish and roast it in a blacksmith's shop,
and eat it with water from the blacksmith's shop,
and drink from the water of the blacksmith's shop.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא – נַיְתֵי בִּינִיתָא וְנִיטְוְויֵיהּ בֵּי נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next backup option in the chain of spleen remedies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roast a fish in a blacksmith's shop, eat it with the blacksmith's water, and drink that water.

steps.title: A goat that drank blacksmith's water had no spleen
steps.stepSummary: A goat used to drink blacksmith's water. When it was slaughtered, it had no spleen at all, which supports the remedy in step 18.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a goat that used to drink water from a blacksmith's shop. When it was slaughtered, no spleen was found in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story as evidence that the blacksmith's-water remedy works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the water could make a goat's spleen disappear completely, it can surely shrink a person's swollen spleen. The story backs up step 18 the same way step 11's story backed up the pepper remedy.
steps.whatToRemember: The spleen cures form a ladder: leeches in wine; goat spleen dried in an oven or between new bricks; the hand of someone who died on שבת; fish and blacksmith's water; and finally a barrel of wine. The goat story backs up the blacksmith's-water cure.

phrases.aramaic: הָהִיא עִיזָּא דַּהֲוָת שָׁתְיָא מַיָּא דְּבֵי נַפָּחָא,
phrases.english: There was a certain goat that used to drink water from a blacksmith's shop;
it was slaughtered, and no spleen was found in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהִיא עִיזָּא דַּהֲוָת שָׁתְיָא מַיָּא דְּבֵי נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the blacksmith's-water remedy of step 18 with a real-life case.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that blacksmith's water shrinks or dries the spleen.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A goat that regularly drank blacksmith's water was found to have no spleen when it was slaughtered.

steps.title: Last spleen remedy: open a barrel of wine
steps.stepSummary: If he cannot do the earlier spleen remedies, he should open a barrel of wine just for himself, meaning he drinks a large amount of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, let him open a barrel of wine for his own sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one last backup cure for the spleen illness: drink a large amount of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the final option in the 'and if not' list that began in step 15. The phrase 'for his sake' means the barrel is opened just for him, so he drinks a lot of it.

keyTerms.meaning: for his sake, just for him

phrases.english: And if not —
let him open a barrel of wine for his sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the final fallback remedy to the spleen list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: As a last resort for a spleen illness, drink a large amount of wine.

steps.title: רב אחא objects: a man with a barrel of wine wouldn't need a doctor
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא tells רב אשי that this remedy makes no sense in practice. Someone who owns a barrel of wine would already be healthy and would never come asking for a cure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא son of רבא said to רב אשי: If he has a barrel of wine, he would not come before the Master in the first place.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בריה דרבא challenges the wine remedy as unrealistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His point is that wine is so good for health that a man who has a whole barrel would never get sick enough to need help. So telling a sick person to drink a barrel is not useful advice. The objection is about how practical the remedy is; he is not saying it is false.

keyTerms.meaning: רב אחא, son of רבא, an אמורא
רב אשי, the leading אמורא of his generation
before the Master, a respectful way of saying 'to you'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
If he has a barrel of wine,
he will not come before the Master.
phrases.notes: He means the wine would already have kept him healthy, so he'd never need to ask you for a cure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wine remedy of step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The barrel-of-wine remedy for the spleen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone rich enough to have a barrel of wine stays healthy from it, so the advice is useless for anyone who actually comes asking for help.

steps.title: A better habit: eat bread every morning
steps.stepSummary: Instead of the wine, רב אחא בריה דרבא suggests a cheap daily habit: eat bread in the morning, because it is good for the whole body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let him get used to eating bread in the morning, because it benefits his entire body.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after his objection, רב אחא offers his own replacement advice: a regular morning meal of bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows he is replacing the expensive wine idea with something anyone can do. Eating in the morning is presented as general health care for the whole body, not only for the spleen.

keyTerms.meaning: get used to, make it a habit

steps.whatToRemember: The spleen remedies end with a practical lesson: a simple habit like eating bread every morning keeps the whole body healthy.

phrases.english: Rather, he should get used to eating bread in the morning,
because it benefits his entire body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the impractical wine remedy with a simple daily habit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating bread every morning benefits the whole body.

steps.title: Remedy for hemorrhoids: a mixture held in a bag
steps.stepSummary: For hemorrhoids (רושחתא), make a mixture of six ingredients and hold it against the sore area in a linen bag in summer or a cotton bag in winter.
steps.simpleTranslation: For hemorrhoids, bring acacia, aloe, mercury, silver dross, a bundle of fragrant herbs, and pigeon droppings. Put them in linen bags in summer, or cotton bags in winter, and hold them on the sore area.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on from the spleen to a new illness, hemorrhoids, and gives a remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cure is a mix of plant, mineral, and animal materials placed on the body. The bag changes with the season: light linen for hot weather, warmer cotton for cold weather.

phrases.english: For hemorrhoids —
let him bring acacia, and aloe,
and mercury, and silver dross,
and a bundle of fragrant herbs,
and pigeon droppings,
and let him hold it in linen bags in the summer,
and in cotton bags in the winter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new illness in the medical list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hemorrhoids are treated with a mixture of ingredients held against the area in a seasonal bag.

steps.title: Backup hemorrhoid remedy: diluted beer
steps.stepSummary: If he cannot prepare the mixture, he should drink diluted beer.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, let him drink diluted beer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a simpler backup option for hemorrhoids.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same 'if not' pattern used for the spleen. If the complicated mixture is not available, an easy drink takes its place.

phrases.english: And if not —
let him drink diluted beer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the fallback for the hemorrhoid remedy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the mixture cannot be used, drink diluted beer for hemorrhoids.

steps.title: Remedy for rheumatism: roll a jar of fish brine on the thighs
steps.stepSummary: For rheumatism (שיגרונא), take a vessel of brine from small fish and roll it sixty times on each thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: For rheumatism, bring a vessel full of brine from small fish and roll it sixty times on this thigh and sixty times on that thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for another illness, rheumatism.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a remedy done on the outside of the body, not eaten. The fixed number, sixty times on each thigh, is part of the instructions.

phrases.english: For rheumatism —
let him bring a vessel of brine from small fish,
and roll it sixty times on this thigh,
and sixty times on that thigh.
phrases.notes: The words are the same as the line before, but now it means the other thigh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next illness in the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rheumatism is treated by rolling a vessel of fish brine sixty times on each thigh.

steps.title: Remedy for a bladder stone: three drops of three liquids
steps.stepSummary: For a bladder stone (צמירתא), mix three drops each of tar oil, leek juice, and clean wine, and apply it to the private area.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a bladder stone, bring three drops of tar oil, three drops of leek juice, and three drops of clean wine, and apply it: for a man on his organ, and for a woman on that place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a remedy for a bladder stone, made from three liquids applied to the outside of the body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern of three drops of each of three liquids is part of the cure. The mixture is placed on the outer private area, and the גמרא uses polite wording for a woman.

phrases.english: For a bladder stone —
let him bring three drops of tar oil,
and three drops of squeezed leek juice,
and three drops of clean wine,
and apply it, for a man on the male organ,
and for a woman on that place.
phrases.notes: 'That place' is a polite way of saying her private area.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the medical list with another illness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bladder stone is treated by applying three drops each of tar oil, leek juice, and clean wine to the private area.

steps.title: First backup cure for a bladder stone: the handle of a wine sac
steps.stepSummary: If the three-drop mixture can't be prepared, hang the handle of a wine sac on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring the handle of a wine sac and hang it: for a man on his private part, for a woman on her breasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a backup cure for the bladder stone (צמירתא) in case the mixture from the last step isn't possible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'וְאִי לָא' tie this step to the remedy before it. This is not a new illness. It is plan B for the same one. The cure is an object you hang on the body, not something you eat or drink.

keyTerms.meaning: And if not (if he can't do the earlier remedy)
A wine sac made of leather

phrases.english: And if not — let him bring the ear of a wine sac,
phrases.notes: The 'ear' is the handle of the leather sac.

phrases.english: and hang it, for a man on his private part,
and for a woman on her breasts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backup remedy for the same bladder stone from step 26
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hang a wine-sac handle on the body as a backup cure for a bladder stone.

steps.title: Second backup cure: a crimson thread
steps.stepSummary: If that isn't possible, hang a crimson thread spun by a woman of bad reputation whose mother had the same reputation.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring a crimson thread spun by a suspected woman who is the daughter of a suspected woman, and hang it: for a man on his private part, for a woman on her breasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another backup cure for the bladder stone. This time the object is a special red thread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The way you hang it is the same as in step 27. Only the object is different. The thread must come from one particular kind of spinner.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman suspected of immoral behavior

phrases.english: And if not — let him bring a crimson thread
spun by a suspected woman, daughter of a suspected woman,
phrases.notes: דּוּמָה is a woman suspected of immoral behavior, and her mother had the same reputation.

phrases.english: and hang it, for a man on his private part
and for a woman on her breasts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next backup in the same list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hang a crimson thread from a suspected woman's daughter as a backup cure.

steps.title: Third backup cure: lice from a man and a woman
steps.stepSummary: If that isn't possible, hang a louse taken from a man and one taken from a woman on the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: If not, bring a louse from a male and from a female and hang it: for a man on his private part, for a woman on that same place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last backup cure for the bladder stone, using lice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the woman's spot changes. It is no longer the breasts but 'that place,' meaning the same area as the man's. As in the earlier backups, the cure is an object hung on the body.

keyTerms.meaning: On that place (a polite way to refer to the private area)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי לָא – לַיְתֵי כִּינָּה דְּזָכָר וּנְקֵבָה,
phrases.english: And if not — let him bring a louse of a male and a female,
phrases.notes: One louse taken from a man and one taken from a woman.

phrases.english: and hang it, for a man on his private part
and for a woman on that place;

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא – לַיְתֵי כִּינָּה דְּזָכָר וּנְקֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final backup in the bladder-stone list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hang lice from a male and a female as a last backup cure.

steps.title: Passing the stone, and using it against fevers
steps.stepSummary: He should urinate on a dry branch by the door pivot and look for the stone that comes out, since it helps against all fevers.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he urinates, let him urinate on a dry branch by the door pivot, and look for the stone that comes out of him. It is good for all fevers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the bladder-stone cure by telling him how to urinate and to save the stone that comes out. It also leads into the next topic: fevers (צימרא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stone itself becomes a cure for fevers. This sets up the next steps, which deal with fevers. Watch out: צִימְרָא (fever) and צְמִירְתָּא (bladder stone) look alike but mean different things.

keyTerms.meaning: The pivot (hinge socket) of a door

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up צְמִירְתָּא (bladder stone, the illness so far) with צִימְרָא (fever, the new topic). The stone from the first illness is used to treat the second.

phrases.english: And when he urinates, let him urinate
on a dry branch by the pivot of the door,
and let him look at the stone that comes out of him,
for it is good for all fevers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the bladder-stone cure and links it to fevers
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinate on a dry branch at the door pivot and keep the stone, since it helps all fevers.

steps.title: Sweat-bath cure for an external fever
steps.stepSummary: Cook date pits and eder leaves separately, sit over the two basins under a table until he heats up, wash, and drink only the eder water.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an external fever: bring three סאה of date pits and three סאה of eder leaves and cook each one separately. Put them in two basins, put a table over himself, and keep moving from sitting over one basin to sitting over the other until he gets hot. Then wash with the water. If he drinks, he should drink the eder water, not the date-pit water, because that causes infertility.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new cure, this time for a fever on the outside of the body (צִימְרָא בָּרָא).
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a steam treatment. The table over him traps the heat, and switching between the basins builds up a sweat. There is one safety rule: don't drink the date-pit water, because it makes a person infertile.

phrases.english: For an external fever —
let him bring three se'ah of date pits,
and three se'ah of eder leaves,
and cook each one separately;
and let him sit between them;
and put them in two basins,
and bring a table and place it over him,

phrases.aramaic: וְנֵיקוּם מֵעִילָּוֵי הַאי וְלֵותֵיב עִילָּוֵי הַאי,
phrases.english: and get up from over this one and sit over that one,
and from over that one sit over this one,
phrases.notes: He keeps switching back and forth between the two basins.

phrases.english: until the heat rises in him;
and let him wash with them,
and when he drinks — let him drink from the eder water,
but let him not drink from the date-pit water;
because it causes infertility.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְצִימְרָא בָּרָא – לַיְתֵי תְּלָתָא גְּרִיבֵי סוּפְלֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from bladder stone to fever, picking up the fever mention in step 30
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweat-bath of date pits and eder leaves for external fever; drink only the eder water.

steps.title: Cure for an internal fever: beets and eder leaves
steps.stepSummary: Cook seven handfuls of beets from seven furrows with their dirt and eat them, then drink eder leaves in beer or (the text continues).
steps.simpleTranslation: For an internal fever: bring seven handfuls of beets from seven furrows, cook them with their dirt, and eat them. Then drink eder leaves in beer, or...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a cure for a fever inside the body (צִימְרָא גַּוְונָא). The sentence breaks off in the middle and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the fever is internal, so the cure is eaten and drunk instead of a steam bath. The eder leaves from the last step show up again, this time mixed into a drink. The word 'אוֹ' (or) tells us another drink option is coming.

phrases.english: For an internal fever —

phrases.aramaic: לַיְתֵי שִׁבְעָה בּוּנֵי דְסִילְקָא מִשַּׁב מְשָׁארֵי,
phrases.english: let him bring seven handfuls of beets from seven furrows,
and cook them with their dirt,
and eat,
and drink eder leaves in beer, or
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going. The other option comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְצִימְרָא גַּוְונָא – לַיְתֵי שִׁבְעָה בּוּנֵי דְסִילְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second kind of fever after the external one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For internal fever, eat beets cooked with their dirt and drink eder leaves in beer (or another option).
